newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FIRST WORLD SERIES GAME PUSHED BACK DUE TO RAIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FIRST WORLD SERIES GAME PUSHED BACK DUE TO RAIN.

text.p: - The opening game of the World Series between the New York Yankees and the Atlanta Braves has been postponed until Sunday night because of heavy rains all day on Saturday in New York, league officials said.
Games One and Two of the 1996 Series will be played on Sunday and on Monday at Yankee Stadium, with the Fall Classic then moving to Atlanta's Fulton County Stadium.

The opening game will begin Sunday at 7:30 p.m. EDT (2330 GMT), and the second game is scheduled for Monday at 7 p.m. (2300 GMT) Games Three, Four and Five in Atlanta will be played as scheduled from Tuesday through Thursday, meaning the teams will play five consecutive days.
Tonight's scheduled starters, Atlanta's John Smoltz and Andy Pettitte of the Yankees, will likely pitch on Sunday.

The delay marks the third time in history that the World Series opener has been postponed. Game One of the 1979 Series between the Pittsburgh Pirates and Baltimore Orioles and the opener of the 1918 World Series between Boston Red Sox and the the Chicago Cubs were postponed due to rain.

The last World Series postponement was due to the San Francisco earthquake in 1989, and the last rainout was in 1986 when Game Seven between the Boston Red Sox and the New York Mets had Game Seven postponed by rain.
